{
  "frontend": {
    "needed": true,
    "prompt": "Implement client-side behavior for the `title` field in create and update flows. Requirements and exact behaviors the frontend must implement (do not rely on backend):

1) Trimming rule (must match backend):
   - Before any client-side validation and before sending the request, remove ONLY leading and trailing U+0020 (ASCII space, code point 0x20). Do not remove other whitespace characters (e.g., \u00A0, \u2003, tabs, newlines).
   - Example JS trimming expression: title.replace(/^[\u0020]+|[\u0020]+$/g, '');

2) Length measurement (must match backend):
   - Measure length by Unicode code points, not bytes or UTF-16 code units.
   - In JavaScript use Array.from(title).length or [...title].length to count code points.

3) Validation rules (client must enforce before submission):
   - Allowed length after trimming: 3 through 80 code points, inclusive.
   - Titles that end up shorter than 3 or longer than 80 must be rejected client-side and not submitted.
   - A title consisting only of U+0020 characters becomes the empty string after trimming and must be rejected.

4) Create (POST /api/v1/items/):
   - title is required. Do not allow form submission without a non-null title that passes trimming+length validation.
   - The payload must include the processed string under the key "title".
   - Do NOT send JSON null for title on create.

5) Update (PUT /api/v1/items/{id}):
   - If the user did not edit the title, omit the title key entirely from the JSON payload so the backend will keep the original.
   - If the user edits the title to a string, apply trimming+validation and send the processed string under "title".
   - If the user attempts to set the title to null (e.g., explicit null value), block this on the client and show a validation error; the backend treats explicit null as 422, so the frontend should never send null.
   - If the user clears the title input to an empty string, run trimming (U+0020-only) and validate; if it fails, show an error and do not submit.

6) Error handling & UX:
   - Surface validation messages that explain: trimmed length must be between 3 and 80 Unicode code points; explicit null is not allowed; all-space strings are invalid.
   - On server 422 responses include the returned validation message; if server returns a processed title in the response body, update the UI if appropriate.

7) Tests / acceptance checks to include in frontend test suite:
   - POST with title "␣ab␣" (U+0020 around) -> trimmed to "ab" -> length 2 -> client rejects and does not submit.
   - POST with title "␣abc␣" -> trimmed to "abc" -> length 3 -> client accepts and submits.
   - POST/PUT with title of 81 code points -> client rejects; 80 code points -> client accepts.
   - Title consisting only of U+0020s -> client rejects.
   - On update, leaving the title input untouched results in payload without title key.

8) Implementation note for HTTP payloads:
   - Send JSON body with key "title" when sending a title string. When omitting title on update, do not include the key at all in the JSON object.

9) Do not assume or change other rules (permissions, description rules). Keep all other API contract aspects unchanged."
  },
  "backend": {
    "needed": true,
    "prompt": "Implement server-side behavior and enforcement for the `title` field for POST /api/v1/items/ and PUT /api/v1/items/{id}. The backend is the source of truth and must enforce all rules regardless of client behavior.

1) Trimming rule (must match frontend):
   - On any incoming request that includes a title value (JSON key present and value is a string), remove ONLY leading and trailing U+0020 (ASCII space, U+0020). Do not trim other Unicode whitespace characters.
   - Example implementations:
     - Node/JS: processed = raw.replace(/^[\u0020]+|[\u0020]+$/g, '');
     - Python: processed = re.sub(r'^[\u0020]+|[\u0020]+$', '', raw)
     - Java: processed = raw.replaceAll("^[\u0020]+|[\u0020]+$", "");
     - Go: use strings.TrimFunc(s, func(r rune) bool { return r == ' ' })

2) Length measurement (server must use Unicode code points):
   - After trimming, count Unicode code points (characters) and validate that length is between 3 and 80 inclusive.
   - Language-specific guidance:
     - Node/JS: length = Array.from(processed).length or [...processed].length
     - Python 3: length = len(processed)
     - Java: length = processed.codePointCount(0, processed.length())
     - Go: length = utf8.RuneCountInString(processed)

3) POST /api/v1/items/ (create):
   - The request MUST include the "title" key with a non-null string value.
   - If title key is missing or is null -> respond 422 Unprocessable Entity.
   - If title is present as a string: apply U+0020 trimming, then validate by code-point length 3..80. If validation fails respond 422 with a clear validation error.
   - On success: store the processed title (the trimmed string) in the persistent item and return responses (201 or as existing API does) containing the stored processed title.

4) PUT /api/v1/items/{id} (update):
   - If the request body does NOT include the title key at all -> do not change the stored title (preserve existing value) and return success if other parts are valid.
   - If the request includes "title":
       - If title is explicit null -> respond 422 Unprocessable Entity (explicit null is always 422).
       - If title is a string -> apply U+0020 trimming and validate by code-point length 3..80. If validation fails respond 422.
       - On success store the processed title and return the updated resource containing the processed title.

5) Error semantics and messages:
   - Use 422 Unprocessable Entity for all validation failures specified above, including explicit null for title.
   - Response body should explain validation failure (e.g., "title must be a string of 3..80 Unicode code points after trimming U+0020; explicit null is not allowed").

6) Storage and responses:
   - Persist the processed (trimmed) title value. Every API response that returns the resource must return the stored processed title (not the raw submitted value).

7) Security and other rules:
   - Do not alter existing permission checks or description rules. Apply permission checks before performing updates/creates as currently implemented.

8) Tests / acceptance checks (server-side test cases to add):
   - POST with JSON {"title": "\u0020ab\u0020"} -> trimmed to "ab" -> length 2 -> respond 422 and do not store.
   - POST with {"title": "\u0020abc\u0020"} -> trimmed to "abc" -> length 3 -> create, stored title == "abc", returned title == "abc".
   - POST with 81 code points -> 422. POST with 80 code points -> success.
   - POST with title consisting only of U+0020s -> trimmed to "" -> 422.
   - PUT without title key -> leave stored title unchanged.
   - PUT with {"title": null} -> 422.
   - PUT with a new string that trims to a valid length -> store trimmed value and return it.

9) Implementation notes:
   - Do validation and trimming in a single canonical place (e.g., request validation layer or model setter) so all code paths (POST, PUT) use identical logic.
   - Log validation failures as appropriate.

10) Do not change or assume other API contract details beyond those stated here. If any additional contract detail is ambiguous or missing (for example, exact error response JSON schema), do not invent it—follow existing project conventions for error payloads."
  }
}
